newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures fall below $23, technically weak.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures fall below $23, technically weak.

text.p: IPE prompt Brent futures fell below $23 for the first time in a month on Friday on a technical move down, traders said.
The front month March contract was trading 38 cents off at $22.69 a barrel at 1110 GMT.
"There's nothing fundamental out there," said one trader. "It's just technically weaker. It's been cooling off for the last two days and it looks like there could be room for further falls."
Key support for the March contract was seen at $22.75 in line with the 40-day moving average and then $22.50 by a number of chartists.
"We feel the market is generally moving sideways at these new "lower" values, and would therefore look to responsively trade this new range," analysts at Mees Pierson said in there daily report.
Some traders said there was a possibility NYMEX would attempt to reverse the fall once it opened.
"I wouldn't go too short just in case NYMEX tries to push back up," said one trader.

The market was continuing to monitor the weather situation in the United States, but many traders said with concerns over heating oil supplies beginning to recede cold weather was no longer such a big issue.
American Petroleum Institute (API) data released on Tuesday showed that year-on-year shortfall in distillate stocks had narrowed to 350,000 barrels from almost 20 million barrels in August.
Leslie Nicholas at commodity brokers GNI, however, warned against complacency concerning stocks.
"There is a general feeling that sufficient supplies exist to cover the winter since stocks are very close to a year ago, but this may be a little complacent," he wrote in his daily bulletin.
"Remember last season when very cold temperatures late in the season caused a run-up in prices?"
